note: Every value is computed at build time from the sources named per insight; components render, never recompute.

insights.question: Most travel is local — but what kind of local?
insights.takeaway: Of 1,440,137 weekday trips by members of Durham households, 56.9% stay inside one municipality, 22.5% cross between Durham municipalities, and 20.6% involve somewhere outside Durham.
insights.universe: All weekday trips by members of Durham households (2022 TTS), wherever they start.
insights.denominatorNote: Denominator: 1,440,137 trips (OD extract total). The three groups are mutually exclusive.
insights.basis: 2022 survey basis (ages 5+, fuller walking capture) — not comparable with pre-2022 trip counts.

sameMunicipality.label: Both endpoints in the same municipality

outsideInvolving.label: At least one endpoint outside Durham

caveats: The third group includes trips made entirely outside Durham by members of Durham households.
Cross-municipality here means both endpoints in Durham but in different municipalities — a Toronto→Whitby trip counts in the third group, not the second.

insights.question: Which relationships make up the internal network?
insights.takeaway: Three connections — Whitby–Oshawa, Oshawa–Clarington, Pickering–Ajax — carry 175,079 two-way trips, 53.9% of all intermunicipal Durham travel.
insights.universe: Weekday trips with both endpoints in Durham but in different municipalities (2022 TTS, Durham households).
insights.denominatorNote: Denominator: 324,532 intermunicipal trips (never the all-trips total).
caveats: These are origin–destination relationships, not observed road corridors or proof of a transit route's demand.
Two-way totals combine both directions; they are not person counts.

insights.question: Does crossing a municipal boundary change the mode mix?
insights.takeaway: Yes, sharply: 56.0% of same-municipality trips are driven vs 76.1% between municipalities, while walking collapses from 14.4% to 0.3%. Trips to Toronto are different again: 15.3% transit.
insights.universe: Weekday trips originating in Durham (2022 TTS, Durham households), by destination context.
insights.denominatorNote: Each context's shares use that context's trip total; contexts are mutually exclusive.
insights.basis: 2022 survey basis. By-mode extract misses 9 mode-not-stated trips region-wide.

contexts.label: Within the same municipality
contexts.description: trips that begin and end in the same Durham municipality

contexts.label: Another Durham municipality
contexts.description: trips that begin in one Durham municipality and end in a different one

contexts.label: Toronto
contexts.description: trips that begin in Durham and end in Toronto

contexts.label: Elsewhere in the survey area
contexts.description: trips that begin in Durham and end outside Durham and Toronto, inside the surveyed area

contexts.label: Beyond the surveyed area
contexts.description: trips that begin in Durham and end outside the surveyed area (TTS code 998)

caveats: This is an association with the destination context, not a causal effect of crossing a boundary.
The former 'Around Durham' context mixed same-municipality and cross-municipality trips; those are separated here.

insights.question: Is everyday travel mostly work travel?
insights.takeaway: No: home-based work is 24.0% of weekday trips by residents, while home-based discretionary travel is 47.0%.
insights.universe: Weekday trips by Durham residents (2022 TTS public summary).
insights.denominatorNote: Denominator: 1,440,149 resident weekday trips (public summary total).
insights.basis: 2022 survey basis; purposes keep their published definitions.
caveats: The published purpose categories sum to 1,440,151 — 2 trips above the published total of 1,440,149. We report categories as published rather than forcing them to match.
Non-home-based is not synonymous with non-work; the remaining ~76% of trips are not 'non-work'.
Trip purposes, not person shares: one person can make several trips of different purposes.

insights.question: Is there one uniform weekday commute?
insights.takeaway: No. Wednesday reports 186,836 people commuting; Friday reports 157,391 — 18.7% more on Wednesday. And 48.6% of those with a known 0–5-day answer commuted 1–4 days.
insights.universe: Persons in the 2022 TTS public summary (Durham Region).
insights.denominatorNote: Day counts: persons reporting commuting each day last week (multiresponse — the same person appears on several days; not five mutually exclusive shares). Frequency: denominator is 263,835 persons with a known 0–5-day response.
caveats: Day-of-week counts describe people reporting each day last week; the same person can appear on several days.
The frequency share excludes 422,549 people in the combined exclusively-home/unemployed category and 5,508 unknown — it is not the share of all employed residents who work hybrid.

insights.question: Did work-at-home change everywhere in the same way?
insights.takeaway: No. Region-wide the share of employed residents usually working at home went from 7.2% (2016) to 14.1% (2022), but municipalities moved in opposite directions.
insights.universe: Employed residents (full-time + part-time, including usually-work-at-home), 2016 and 2022 TTS.
insights.denominatorNote: Denominator: employed persons. A share is computed only when every employment cell is observed.
insights.basis: Employment measures are collected comparably in 2016 and 2022.
caveats: Point estimates from two survey cycles; no statistical significance is claimed and the survey cannot say why the change happened.
1986 is not part of this comparison: its part-time-at-home cell is suppressed, so no defensible value exists.

insights.question: Where was the comparable transit decline concentrated?
insights.takeaway: On the 2016-comparable basis, the transit share fell in all 7 municipalities with computable 2016 cells (Brock's 2016 transit components are suppressed, so its change is not computable). Region-wide the comparable total moved 1.5% while the transit share went from 6.4% to 3.9%.
insights.universe: 2016: resident weekday trips (public summary). 2022: trips by Durham households on the 2016-comparable basis (excl2016 = 0 extract).
insights.denominatorNote: Each year's share uses that year's comparable trip total. Sources differ by 12–18 trips at region level; differences are documented, not forced.
insights.basis: Harmonized comparison basis (excl2016 = 0). Never mix with full-basis 2022 shares.

municipalities.name: Brock
municipalities.status2016: not computable from 2016 published cells (suppressed transit component)

caveats: 2022 reflects a post-pandemic travel environment; the survey alone cannot attribute causes.
The 2016 figures come from the public summary; the 2022 comparable figures from the iDRS extract — reconciliation differences between extracts are documented, not eliminated.
Municipality = municipality of household for the 2022 extract.

insights.question: Has demographic change altered the context?
insights.takeaway: Durham's surveyed population aged 65+ went from 13.3% (2016) to 15.5% (2022); households grew 8.4% while vehicles per known household moved 1.83 → 1.81.
insights.universe: All residents and households in the Durham survey (2016 and 2022 TTS).
insights.denominatorNote: 65+ share uses all residents; vehicles per household is a mean over known households with '5 or more' counted as 5.
insights.basis: Household/person measures; broadly stable definitions with documented cycle changes.
caveats: These are community-level associations; marginal tables cannot establish joint demographic behaviour (no income × age × vehicle-access inference).
The shared top-code assumption biases vehicle means low, and the bias need not be equal across communities or cycles.

unavailable.question: Joint demographic behaviour (e.g. low-income seniors without cars)
unavailable.reason: The published files are marginal tables; municipality-level percentages cannot establish joint population behaviour. Requires the cross-tabulated extracts specified in docs/acquisition-manifest.md (Q05).

unavailable.question: Routes used, travel times, emissions, feasible mode shift
unavailable.reason: Desire lines show only where trips begin and end; no path, time or emissions data exists in the extracts.

unavailable.question: Inbound travel by non-Durham households
unavailable.reason: The authorized extracts cover trips by members of Durham households only. Requires extract Q02 (all surveyed households with a Durham endpoint).

unavailable.question: Sample reliability / confidence intervals for OD flows
unavailable.reason: Unexpanded support counts were not part of the extracts; expanded counts are estimates and standard errors must not be invented. Requires extract Q01.
